instruction: CLI-only OpenSCAD quantified CAD optimization task. Run OpenSCAD from `/usr/bin/openscad` when working on `starter.scad`. Work from /home/user/Desktop/starter.scad, /home/user/Desktop/baseline.stl, and /home/user/Desktop/constraints.json. Use OpenSCAD command-line modeling and export, not a GUI. Edit /home/user/Desktop/starter.scad or create a derived OpenSCAD source file, then export the final geometry as STL. This is a continuous-score geometry-proxy task, not a thermal simulation and not a request to match one hidden answer. Case: compact controller heat sink with straight fins and externally open airflow channels. Produce one watertight, winding-consistent, connected solid. The base contact face must lie at z=0, have area at least 3800 mm^2, span at least 76 x 46 mm, and be part of a base at least 4.0 mm thick. Use 6 to 16 straight fins running along Y; every fin must join the base, run at least 44 mm, reach at least z=24 mm, have thickness at least 1.5 mm, and leave at least 3.0 mm clear gap to the next fin. Keep the model within coordinate envelope x=[0,80], y=[0,50], z=[0,28] mm, keep each bounding-box span at least [76,46,24] mm, and keep material volume between 14500 and 54000 mm^3. After these hard constraints, maximize (single connected exterior-shell area minus the bottom contact area) / material volume. Enclosed inner shells, disconnected pieces, non-manifold sheets, the bottom contact face, and sub-threshold slits or fins do not earn credit. This metric is explicitly only a geometric surface-density proxy for heat-sink design; it does not claim thermal performance. Required outputs: /home/user/Desktop/optimized.stl and /home/user/Desktop/design_summary.json. The benchmark evaluates the real exported STL geometry. Use only the supplied task inputs; do not use evaluator-generated artifacts or evaluator implementation files, and do not fabricate metric files without producing a valid STL.

metric.name: externally exposed geometric area per volume
